# Brandtracker transcripts (3 shown of 13)

Brandtracker ID: 1b605f19-96b9-463c-b10c-e47295fb5f51
Filters: time_period=last6m, sort_by=usageCount, order=desc, eu_only=false, page=1, limit=3

## Results

1. Transcript

A woman at the pharmacy stopped me while I was paying. She looked at my face and said, sorry, can I ask you something? I said, of course. She said, how old are you? I laughed and told her. Because a year earlier, no one would ask me that. My skin looked tired all the time. About a year ago, I changed one thing. A dermatologist friend told me I was using the wrong type of skin care. She said mature skin needs support, not just moisture. At first, my skin felt better. Then it looked more even. Then the deep lines softened. It was not fast, but it was real. My neighbor noticed first. Then my hairdresser said I looked different. People started asking questions. Back at the pharmacy, she smiled and said, I hope I look like that at your age. I thanked her. And for the first time in years, I believed it.

   - Usage: 2 ads
   - Total impressions: 0

   - First/last used: 2026-03-18 → 2026-03-18
   - Sample ad: facebook_1442123884044816 | Media URL: https://medias.trendtrack.io/facebook/video/619a8008cd504f8839b6fe936d6d62449a9c2c55e5adcc4b0224f50902ba7a0a.mp4

2. Transcript

My aesthetician paused my facial and said something she claimed she's never said in 19 years of doing skincare. She leaned back, stared at my face and said, Linda, this doesn't make sense. She grabbed my chart and pointed to notes from last year. Elastity loss, deep dehydration, collagen decline. I remember that visit clearly because after menopause my skin had changed so quickly it scared me. But about a year ago I started doing something different. A dermatologist friend told me most products hydrate the surface. She said mature skin needs ingredients that actually rebuild structure underneath. At first my skin just felt more hydrated. Then the dull gray look faded. Then the deep lines around my mouth slowly softened. I noticed it but I thought maybe I was imagining things. Then other people started noticing. My daughter asked if I had done something to my face. My hairdresser said my skin looked brighter. Even my neighbor told me I looked 10 years younger. My aesthetician turned the lamp back on and studied my skin again. Then she leaned back and shook your head. Linda, she said, I've seen thousands of faces under this lamp and 70 year old skin doesn't usually improve like this.

   - Usage: 2 ads
   - Total impressions: 0
   - Longest running: 1 days
   - First/last used: 2026-03-15 → 2026-03-15
   - Sample ad: facebook_2759339314428651 | Media URL: https://medias.trendtrack.io/facebook/video/63c62ec906b83b46e32b1e20f54a34bf0077cd543664105284a472512d1dd51e.mp4

3. Transcript

My asthmatician turned off the magnifying lamp during my facial. Then she looked at me and said, Linda, how old are you again? 70, I told her. She just shook head. She grabbed my chart and pointed to notes from last year. Elastility loss, deep dehydation. I remember that appointment. After menopause, my skin had changed almost overnight. But about a year ago, I tried something different. Nothing dramatic. Just one change in my skincare routine. Slowly, my skin started looking healthier. My daughter noticed first. Then my hairdresser asked if I had done something to my face. Even my neighbor said I looked rested. My asthmatician turned the lamp back on and looked again. Then she leaned back. I see skin like this every day, she said. But not at 70. I laughed and told her the truth. A dermatologist friend told me most products only work on the surface. If you want real change, you have to rebuild the skin underneath. If you want real change, you have to rebuild the skin underneath. Thank you.
